title: Right move at the right boundary
statement: For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, moving the input head one position to the right from position $n+1$, the rightmost of the $n+2$ allowed positions, leaves it at position $n+1$.
replaced:
On an input of length $n$, attempting to move the input head right (by the sign $1$)
from the rightmost position $n + 1$ results in no movement: the clamped move of $n + 1$
by $1$ is again $n + 1$.
